content: Need to add rate limiting to our public API. We've been running without it and last week a partner's integration bug sent us 50K requests per second for an hour. Our services handled it fine but the database connection pool was completely saturated.

Rate limiting at the API gateway level would prevent this. You'd want per-API-key limits (e.g., 100 req/s per partner) plus a global limit as a safety net. Redis-based token bucket or sliding window algorithms are the standard approach.

Token bucket is my preference — it allows bursts up to the bucket capacity while enforcing the average rate. I'll implement it in our Envoy gateway using the rate limit service pattern. The thing is, I also need different tiers — our premium partners get 500 req/s, standard gets 100, trial gets 20.
You can map API key → tier in your auth layer and pass the tier as a header to the rate limit service. The rate limit service then applies the appropriate bucket configuration for that tier.

Right. And I want to return proper 429 responses with Retry-After headers so well-behaved clients know when to back off. The partner that hammered us was actually retry-storming because their error handling treated 500s as transient and retried immediately with no backpressure.
That's a classic retry storm. Rate limiting from your side protects you, but documenting exponential backoff with jitter in your API docs would help partners build more resilient integrations.

Fundamentally this is a contract between us and our partners — we guarantee capacity up to the rate limit, they agree to respect 429s and back off. Without that contract it's just two systems fighting each other.
